title: Building Better Sleep Habits
hook: Good sleep is mostly built in the hours before bed. A handful of simple habits — collectively called sleep hygiene — do more than any gadget.
key_points: Keep a consistent schedule: same bedtime and wake time, even on weekends.
Keep the bedroom dark, quiet, cool, and screen-free.
Avoid caffeine, big meals, and alcohol close to bedtime.
Wind down with a relaxing routine, and get daylight and activity during the day.
content_html: If you struggle to fall or stay asleep, the fix usually isn't a supplement — it's the environment and routine you build around bedtime. Sleep specialists call this "sleep hygiene," and it's the first thing they recommend.
extra_html: The NHS advises keeping a regular sleep schedule — the same bedtime and wake time every day — so your internal clock knows what to expect. The bedroom should be dark, quiet, cool, and free of phones and screens, whose light and pull keep the brain alert. In the hours before bed, skip caffeine, heavy meals, and alcohol (which fragments sleep even though it makes you drowsy). A calming wind-down routine — a warm bath, reading, dimmed lights — signals the body to power down. During the day, daylight exposure and physical activity strengthen the rhythm that makes nighttime sleep come more easily. None of it is dramatic, but stacked together these habits are what reliably move the needle.

related.title: Why Sleep Matters
related.hook: Sleep isn't downtime — it's when your brain consolidates memory and your body repairs itself. Skimp on it for long and the bill comes due in your health.

related.title: Building Everyday Resilience
related.hook: Resilience isn't a personality you're born with — it's a set of habits and connections you can build, the way you build a muscle.

flashcards.prompt: What single habit does most to anchor a healthy sleep rhythm?
flashcards.back_html: A consistent schedule — going to bed and waking up at the same times, including weekends, trains your body clock.

flashcards.prompt: Which is recommended for better sleep?

choices.text: A dark, quiet, cool, screen-free bedroom
A nightcap of alcohol before bed
Scrolling your phone until you feel sleepy

flashcards.explanation_html: A dark, quiet, cool room supports sleep, while alcohol and late screen time both disrupt it.
